change_in_accounting_principle.definition: Change from one GAAP method to another GAAP method
examples: Completed contract to percentage of completion
change_in_accounting_principle.treatment: RETROSPECTIVE application (restate prior periods as if new principle always used)
change_in_accounting_principle.disclosure: Reason for change, method of applying change, effect on income

change_in_accounting_estimate.definition: Change based on NEW information or experience (not an error)
examples: Change in useful life of asset
Change in allowance for doubtful accounts
change_in_accounting_estimate.treatment: PROSPECTIVE application (current and future periods only, NO restatement)

change_in_reporting_entity.definition: Change resulting in financial statements of different entity
examples: Change in subsidiaries in consolidated group
change_in_reporting_entity.treatment: RETROSPECTIVE application (restate all prior periods presented)

retrospective.when_used: Change in principle, change in reporting entity, error corrections
retrospective.how: Restate prior period financial statements as if new method always used
retrospective.adjustment: Adjust beginning retained earnings of earliest period presented for cumulative effect
retrospective.disclosure: Show effect of change on prior periods

prospective.when_used: Change in estimate, some specific principle changes (e.g., depreciation method change treated as estimate change)
prospective.how: Apply new estimate to current and future periods only
prospective.example: Change useful life from 10 to 8 years: Use remaining book value and depreciate over remaining 8 years going forward

impracticability_exception.if_impracticable: If retrospective application impracticable (cannot determine cumulative effect), apply prospectively from earliest date practicable

calculation_example_principle.scenario: Company changes from FIFO to weighted average on Jan 1, Year 3. Prior years: Year 1 FIFO COGS $100K (weighted avg would have been $110K), Year 2 FIFO COGS $120K (weighted avg would have been $130K). Tax rate 30%.
cumulative_effect_calculation: Year 1 effect: COGS increased $10K → NI decreased $7K after tax
Year 2 effect: COGS increased $10K → NI decreased $7K after tax
Cumulative effect on RE at start of Year 3: $14K decrease (after tax)
calculation_example_principle.retrospective_adjustment: DR Retained Earnings $14K (cumulative after-tax effect), CR Inventory $20K (cumulative pretax), DR Deferred Tax Asset $6K (tax effect: $20K × 30%)
calculation_example_principle.restatement: Restate Year 1 and Year 2 financial statements to show weighted average COGS and lower NI
calculation_example_principle.year_3_forward: Use weighted average method going forward

calculation_example_estimate.scenario: Equipment cost $100K, originally estimated 10-year life, $10K salvage. After 4 years (BV = $64K), change estimate to 12-year total life. No change to salvage.
calculation_example_estimate.new_estimate: Total life 12 years, already used 4 years, 8 years remaining
calculation_example_estimate.no_adjustment_to_prior_years: Do NOT restate Years 1-4. Just use new depreciation rate prospectively.
calculation_example_estimate.journal_entry_year_5: DR Depreciation Expense $6,750, CR Accumulated Depreciation $6,750

indirect_effects.definition: Changes to current or future cash flows resulting from change in principle
examples: Bonus arrangements affected by restated income
indirect_effects.treatment: Report in period of change, do NOT restate prior periods

depreciation_method_change.unique_treatment: Treated as change in ESTIMATE, not principle
depreciation_method_change.reason: Change in estimate of pattern of consumption

inventory_method_change.common_on_exam: FIFO to weighted average or vice versa

long_term_contract_method.example: Completed contract to percentage of completion

error_corrections_comparison.error: Mistake in prior period → RESTATE prior periods, adjust beginning RE
error_corrections_comparison.change_in_estimate: NOT a mistake, new information → PROSPECTIVE, no restatement
error_corrections_comparison.change_in_principle: Voluntary change between GAAP methods → RETROSPECTIVE restatement

cpa_exam_tips: Principle = Retrospective (restate prior periods). Estimate = Prospective (going forward only).
Error corrections look like retrospective principle changes but are CORRECTIONS not voluntary changes
Depreciation method change = treated as ESTIMATE (prospective), not principle
Cumulative effect goes to beginning Retained Earnings of earliest period presented
If they say 'new information' or 'based on experience' → change in ESTIMATE (prospective)
If they say 'company decided to switch from X to Y' → change in PRINCIPLE (retrospective)

principle_keywords: change from FIFO to weighted average

retrospective_steps: 1. Calculate what prior years' income WOULD have been under new method
2. Calculate cumulative after-tax effect on retained earnings
3. Adjust beginning RE of earliest period presented
prospective_steps: 1. Take current book value (or carrying amount)
2. Apply new estimate going forward (new life, new salvage, etc.)

common_traps: Don't restate prior periods for change in estimate (prospective only)
Don't confuse depreciation method change (estimate treatment) with inventory method change (principle treatment)
Remember to calculate AFTER-TAX cumulative effect for principle changes
Don't forget to adjust deferred taxes when restating for principle change

key_points: Change in principle = Retrospective restatement (adjust beginning RE, restate prior periods)
Change in estimate = Prospective application (current and future periods only)
Error corrections = Restate prior periods like retrospective principle change
Depreciation method change treated as ESTIMATE (prospective) not principle
Cumulative effect on beginning RE calculated after-tax
